rules.rule:
Read .github/review-criteria.md and apply it in full. It names CLAUDE.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-ecommerce-architecture-design.md; read both before reporting anything.

This is production Java. Report only what you can point at a line for.

- @Component, @Service and @Repository are forbidden. @RestController and @RestControllerAdvice are the only stereotypes and only in the controller layer. Every other bean is an @Bean method in an @Configuration class. Spring Data JPA repository interfaces are the one exception.
- Layering is controller then service then repository then jpa. The controller speaks Request and Response records, the service speaks models, the repository returns models, the jpa layer owns entities. Service and repository each have an interface plus an Impl beside it in the same package; there is no impl subpackage. @Transactional and caching live on the service.
- Spring Data derived query methods are the default. @Query is allowed only where a derived method cannot express the query, and its text must be standard JPQL. Anything JPQL has no syntax for, such as a recursive CTE, a set operation or a window function, must carry nativeQuery = true and be ANSI SQL. A provider extension such as Hibernate HQL is a finding, and so is a Criteria string fragment.
- Boundary records are named for the entity and never the operation: CategoryRequest, never CreateCategoryRequest or UpdateCategoryRequest, and one request type per entity. Lookups are prefixed find at every layer; mutations use verbs. Private methods come last, after every other method.
- Constraints live on Request records only; entities carry none. Constraints guard shape. Integrity stays in the database, so uniqueness is a 409 and never a field error.
- No value-object wrappers such as Money, Price, Sku or Slug. Money is a bare BigDecimal compared with compareTo. Identifiers are UUID on entities and String at every layer above.
- Models are Lombok classes rather than records unless genuinely read-only.
- No comments and no Javadoc. A comment is a finding; the fix is to rewrite the code, and rationale belongs in the spec.
- Nothing built that the issue did not ask for: no helper classes, DTOs or configuration knobs nobody requested.

Read .github/review-criteria.md and apply it in full. It names CLAUDE.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-ecommerce-architecture-design.md; read both before reporting anything.

Tests are reviewed here because TDD is a standing rule rather than an aspiration.

- Every behaviour added by the production code in this diff needs a test that would have failed before it: a branch, a loop, validation, orchestration, arithmetic, an HTTP contract. Production behaviour with nothing failing behind it is a finding.
- Code with no behaviour gets no test. A test for a MapStruct mapper, a Lombok accessor, an exception that only extends RuntimeException, an entity field, or an @Bean method that calls a constructor is a finding, and so is any test that asserts what the framework does rather than what this code does.
- Test methods are named givenContext_whenMethod_thenResult, where the middle part is the method under test. The find prefix rule is about production lookups and does not reach test names.
- No comments.
- Do not comment on formatting.

Read .github/review-criteria.md and apply it in full. It names CLAUDE.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-ecommerce-architecture-design.md; read both before reporting anything.

Migrations and configuration.

- No comments in SQL, YAML, properties files or shell scripts. A comment is a finding.
- Integrity belongs here rather than in Java. Uniqueness, foreign keys and defaults are the database's job, and a Java guard that duplicates one is a read-then-write race the constraint has to catch anyway.
- Money is numeric(19,3). Identifiers are uuid holding UUIDv7.
- Never write a configuration key that already holds the value you want.
- Raw SQL belongs in Flyway migrations and nowhere else. A migration that has already been applied is never edited; a change to one is a finding unless the diff also shows the database being rebuilt from scratch.
